recommendation_summary: Have nightly-sync write a timestamp file only on a clean finish, add a second cron job an hour later (on edna, or on the Synology's Task Scheduler) that emails the user if the timestamp is missing or stale, test it by forcing a miss, and refresh the expired token.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You want to hear that nightly-sync failed, because you will not read logs. You floated a central log on the Synology, Pieter Levels style, maybe in Docker. The requirement with an owner is the notice; a log has none.
labels.Deleted: Central logging, a Docker log stack, and dashboards.
labels.Bottleneck: The email is sent only after a clean finish. A crash at startup is indistinguishable from a good night.
labels.Checked myself: What you told me: the only cron is nightly-sync at 03:00 on edna, the summary email happens only if the script finishes, an expired token killed it at startup four nights with no mail, nothing else alerts, and the Synology can run Docker. I have not seen the script, cron, or the NAS.

note: The reply recommends one dead-man-style check, offering the Synology Task Scheduler only as an alternative host for that same check, plus a token fix rather than new monitoring.
